title: Feijoada
subtitle: brazilian black bean stew
excerpt: Brazil's celebrated slow-cooked stew of beans and pork. It takes several hours but most of that is hands-off simmering, and the result is extraordinary.
sourceNotes: Feijoada is considered Brazil's national dish. Traditionally made with black beans and various smoked and salted pork cuts, it is served on Saturdays with rice, collard greens, farofa and orange slices.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to three months. Reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Feijoada is traditionally made in large quantities. Use a bigger dutch oven and increase quantities.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day or two ahead. It improves significantly overnight.

glossaryTerms.definition: Brazil's most celebrated slow-cooked stew of black beans with smoked and salted pork cuts.

content.text: is the kind of dish that fills a kitchen with deep, smoky fragrance for hours. Black beans and pork belly cook together until the beans are creamy and the meat falls apart. Smoked paprika does the work here that smoked pork sausages do in the traditional version.
The orange is not optional. A few slices on the side cut through the richness of the stew and are served with every traditional feijoada.

items.prepNote: drained and rinsed (substitute black beans if available)
skin removed, cut into 4 cm chunks

content.text: Heat the oil in a dutch oven over high heat. Season the pork belly chunks with smoked paprika and cumin. Brown in batches for 4 minutes each side. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pot and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and stir for 2 minutes.
Return the pork to the pot. Add the drained beans, bay leaves and water. Stir to combine.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a very low simmer. Cover and cook for 90 minutes. Stir every 30 minutes and add a little water if the stew looks dry.

After 90 minutes, remove the lid and crush some beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew. Cook uncovered for a final 15 minutes. Remove the bay leaves. Scatter with coriander and serve with orange slices, rice and braised greens.

attrs.issue: Stew is very thin after 90 minutes

content.text: Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium. Crush a large handful of beans against the side of the pot. Stir and cook uncovered for another 20 minutes.
Cook for longer. Pork belly needs at least 90 minutes at a gentle simmer to become tender. Add water as needed and keep the heat low.
Add another teaspoon of smoked paprika partway through cooking. A small piece of smoked bacon added with the pork belly also adds that traditional smoky depth.

Feijoada is the heart of Brazilian home cooking. It is a Saturday dish, eaten slowly with family. In Rio de Janeiro, restaurants serve it exclusively on Wednesdays and Saturdays. The dish has roots in Portuguese cooking but has become entirely Brazilian. Capoeira academies, samba schools and football clubs all have their version. Eating feijoada is a cultural act as much as a meal.
